title: Worksheet — Resources and Development (Class 10 CBSE Geography)
instructions: Attempt all 11 questions. Show your reasoning where required. Total time: 50 minutes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a BIOTIC resource?
Coal and petroleum are classified as:
questions.explanation: Take millions of years to form.

questions.question: Black soil is also called regur and is good for cotton.
The Earth Summit at Rio was held in the year ____.
India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends up to:
Major cause of land degradation in Punjab, Haryana, western UP:
options: over-irrigation leading to water-logging and salinity
questions.answer: over-irrigation leading to water-logging and salinity

questions.question: Classify resources on the basis of EXHAUSTIBILITY with two examples each.
questions.answer: (i) RENEWABLE — can be renewed by natural processes; e.g. solar energy, wind, water, forests, wildlife. (ii) NON-RENEWABLE — take millions of years to form; e.g. coal, petroleum, most metallic minerals.

questions.question: What is sustainable development? What was Agenda 21?
questions.answer: SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT means development that takes place without damaging the environment, and that does not compromise the needs of future generations. AGENDA 21 is a global declaration signed at the UNCED Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro in 1992 — a global plan of action to combat environmental damage, poverty and disease through global cooperation. Every local government is expected to draw its own LOCAL AGENDA 21.

questions.question: Compare BLACK soil and LATERITE soil — region, formation, fertility, suitable crops.
questions.answer: BLACK SOIL — Deccan trap (Maharashtra, MP, Saurashtra, Malwa, Chhattisgarh) on basalt lava; rich in calcium, magnesium, potash, lime; holds moisture; ideal for COTTON, also pulses and millets. LATERITE SOIL — high-temperature, high-rainfall regions (Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, MP, Odisha, Assam hills); intense leaching removes lime and silica leaving iron and aluminium; LOW humus; needs manures + fertilisers; suitable for tea, coffee, cashew nut.

questions.question: Explain different methods of soil conservation. Discuss with at least four examples.
questions.answer: (i) CONTOUR PLOUGHING — ploughing along contour lines decelerates water flow on slopes and reduces erosion. (ii) TERRACE CULTIVATION — cutting steps on hill slopes turns them into level fields; used in the Himalayas. (iii) STRIP CROPPING — strips of grass between strips of crop break the force of wind and water. (iv) SHELTER BELTS — rows of trees slow wind and have stabilised sand dunes in western India. (v) Afforestation, controlled grazing, mining control, and treatment of industrial effluents complete the picture. Together these methods conserve topsoil, retain moisture and keep land productive.

questions.question: Why is resource conservation essential for sustainable development? Discuss with reference to the Earth Summit and at least two specific challenges India faces.
questions.answer: INDISCRIMINATE use of resources concentrates them in a few hands, creates inequality between 'haves' and 'have-nots', and has produced global ecological crises — global warming, ozone depletion, pollution, land degradation. SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT (Brundtland) means development that meets present needs without compromising future generations. The 1992 EARTH SUMMIT at Rio brought together over 100 heads of state; they signed declarations on climate change and biodiversity, and AGENDA 21 — a global plan to combat environmental damage and poverty. INDIAN CHALLENGES: (a) very uneven distribution — Jharkhand mineral-rich, Rajasthan solar-rich but water-poor, Arunachal water-rich but infrastructure-poor — so RESOURCE PLANNING by survey + structure + national integration is essential. (b) LAND DEGRADATION (130 million ha) from mining, over-grazing and over-irrigation — addressed by afforestation, shelter belts, terrace farming, controlled mining. Conservation is therefore both an environmental imperative and a development necessity.
